title: Evaluation of Digital Initial Assessment and Clinical Triage - A prospective, non-randomised, controlled real-world evidence study conducted in a emergency department using a mixed-methods design
summary:
Background:
Emergency departments in Germany are increasingly overcrowded and operating at or beyond capacity. A large proportion of patients do not require urgent hospital-based treatment. Digital symptom checkers could help guide patients to the level of care most appropriate for their needs.

Research Question:
The study aims to investigate whether and how the digital recommendation provided by the symptom checker “Docyet” can influence patients’ subsequent use of healthcare services. In addition, the use of healthcare resources and patients’ experiences will be evaluated.

Methods:
The study is conducted under real-world conditions of routine care in the Emergency Department of Klinikum Fulda. The digital assessment is compared with an expert assessment, and patients’ subsequent decisions and further healthcare pathways are observed.
conditions: Overcrowding of emergency departments due to a high proportion of non-urgent patient presentations. The study investigates whether a digital symptom checker (Docyet) can contribute to directing patients to the appropriate level of care according to their healthcare needs, using real-world data from routine care.

interventions.name:
Prospective observation of patients who use the digital symptom checker 'Docyet' independently to assess their symptoms initially.

Data collection 1: One-off completion of the digital questionnaire (chatbot medical history) prior to clinical triage (duration: approximately 5–8 minutes).

Control group not exposed to the digital application.

- Study: One-time data extraction from the hospital information systems (eCare/Medico) to collect baseline parameters (e.g., urgency level/ESI level, extent of diagnostic work-up, duration of treatment).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
General criteria (both groups):
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Independent attendance at the emergency Department (self-referral)
- Presentation with a medical complaint
- Sufficient command of the German language (software and documentation are available exclusively in German)

Additional criteria for the intervention group (Group A):
- Verifiable use of the Symptom Checker
- The symptom checker is used for the participant themselves
- Full completion of the digital questionnaire (up to the recommendation)
- Provision of informed consent for data linkage

- For the follow-up subgroups: Opt-in given for telephone contact or the guideline-based interview.

Additional criteria for the control group (Group B):
- Visit to the emergency department during the same study period as Group A
- No use of the symptom checker for the current visit
- Availability of clinical patient documentation
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients with immediately life-threatening conditions or requiring urgent treatment
- Patients who were not admitted independently (‘self-referral’) but were brought in via the ambulance service or an emergency doctor
- People under 18 years of age
- Patients who are unable to provide informed consent (dementia, acute psychosis, severe intoxication)
